sources.topic: AACE cost estimate classification (generic 17R-97 and process industries 18R-97)
sources.title: Professional Guidance Document No. 01 - Guide to Cost Estimate Classification Systems (Rev. August 29, 2022); it indexes RP 17R-97 and RP 18R-97 (Cost Estimate Classification System - As Applied in Engineering, Procurement, and Construction for the Process Industries)
sources.edition_or_publication_date: PGD 01 Rev. August 29, 2022 (the RP texts 17R-97 / 18R-97 themselves were NOT opened; member download / paid)
sources.clause_or_page: PGD 01 sections: Introduction; Classification Concepts and Principles; Guide entries 17R-97 and 18R-97
sources.scope: Guide to AACE's estimate-classification recommended practices: five classes, Class 5 (least defined) to Class 1 (most defined); 17R-97 is the generic principles RP; 18R-97 is the process-industries application.
sources.limitations: Verified from AACE's own guidance document about the RPs, not from the text of 17R-97 or 18R-97. Copyrighted; RP text is member/paid. Class definitions, maturity percentages and accuracy ranges in the RPs were not read and must not be copied from memory.
sources.paraphrase: AACE describes five estimate classes (5 to 1, least to most defined). Per PGD 01, the maturity of scope definition is the primary determinant of class; end use, method, effort and accuracy are secondary. Accuracy ranges are indicative and not targets.
sources.notes: PGD 01 is a primary AACE publication but only a pointer to the RPs, hence 'Partially verified'. Class purposes (e.g. Class 5 concept screening ... Class 1 check estimate) were NOT read on the AACE page and are not recorded; a person must acquire 17R-97/18R-97 to record them. The PGD notes class is not a contract specification for estimate quality. Never present accuracy percentages from memory.

sources.topic: AACE cost estimate classification - building and general construction (56R-08)
sources.title: 56R-08: Cost Estimate Classification System - As Applied in Engineering, Procurement, and Construction for the Building and General Construction Industries
sources.edition_or_publication_date: RP number suffix -08 as listed; current revision date of the RP not seen (RP text not opened)
sources.clause_or_page: PGD 01 'Guide to Industry Specific Estimate Classification RPs' entry for 56R-08
sources.scope: As listed by AACE: new or renovated buildings plus repetitive site/civil projects (e.g. site development, utilities, water and sewer pipelines); excludes process industries, road/rail, hydropower, tunnels, and one-of-a-kind special facilities.
sources.limitations: RP text not read (member download / non-member purchase). Only AACE's scope summary seen. Copyrighted.
sources.paraphrase: AACE's guide lists 56R-08 as the building and general construction application of its five-class estimate classification, covering buildings and repeatable site/civil work, with listed exclusions for process, transport, hydropower and unique special-purpose facilities.
sources.notes: Most relevant AACE RP for a building-led KSA contractor; for oil and gas/process packages 18R-97 applies, and PGD 01 says mixed-scope projects should rate each WBS element with the most suitable RP. Human must buy/obtain RP text before the tool states class criteria.

sources.topic: Saudi Labor Law - normal hours, Ramadan hours, overtime premium, weekly rest
sources.title: Actually working hours (HRSD Knowledge Centre, Labor Education); Overtime Hours (HRSD Knowledge Centre)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (HRSD / MHRSD)
sources.edition_or_publication_date: HRSD Knowledge Centre pages authored 15 November 2019 (18 Rabi' Al-Awwal 1441); browser prints of the pages supplied by the project owner on 2026-10-17 (2 pp. + 1 p.)
sources.clause_or_page: Labor Law Arts. 98, 99, 100, 107 as quoted on 'Actually working hours' (also Arts. 113 and 151 on leave); 'Overtime Hours' page cites Executive Regulations Art. 22 for the annual overtime figure
sources.scope: Max actual working hours per day/week, reduced Ramadan hours for Muslims, overtime pay, overtime on public holidays.
sources.limitations: HRSD educational summary, superseded for the legal text by STD-014 (Labor Law read directly: Arts. 98-107 confirmed, including Art. 100 whose HRSD print was unclear). Executive Regulations (Art. 22 overtime ceiling) still not read. Applicability to non-Muslims, industries and Minister decisions (Art. 99) must be checked by a person.
sources.paraphrase: HRSD pages state: actual work up to 8 h/day or 48 h/week, reduced in Ramadan for Muslims to 6/36 (Art. 98); 9 h/day for some categories or 7 h for hazardous work per Ministerial decision (Art. 99); rotation work averaged over <=3 weeks with Ministry approval (Art. 100); overtime = hourly wage + 50% of basic wage, hours on public holidays are overtime (Art. 107); overtime page cites 720 extra hours/year (Exec. Regs Art. 22).
sources.notes: Evidence files (local, not committed): data/standards/evidence/HRSD_Actually_working_hours_Labor_Law_Arts_98-107_printed_2026-10-17.pdf sha256 e577023c2d02041a5c151cfb3c85b1c1f42c5c95eca92120ce2a8908b3905fe2; data/standards/evidence/HRSD_Overtime_hours_printed_2026-10-17.pdf sha256 8d4a60aa19ce9c814128a5d421d408f3578e2ccf7ced835da7fd1c38a8b7fd7f. Treat as an official ministry summary; a person should confirm against the current Labor Law and Executive Regulations. Use only as sources for governed parameters, never as hard-coded defaults.

sources.title: Value Added Tax (ZATCA Rules and Regulations page) and Guideline for Amendments to the Implementing Regulation of Value Added Tax
sources.edition_or_publication_date: Guideline for Amendments to the Implementing Regulation of VAT, Issue 1, April 2025 (explains ZATCA Board Resolution No. 01-06-24 of 19 November 2024); 47-page PDF supplied by the project owner on 2026-10-17; English for guidance, Arabic prevails
sources.clause_or_page: Guideline s.1.3 (p.6: VAT charged at 15% where applicable); 15% also appears at p.27 (electricity example) and p.30 (worked example); contents: tax groups, cessation, supply of services, deemed supply, transfer of activity, VAT suspension, services to non-GCC residents, subsidies, financing contracts, electronic marketplaces, restricted purchases, return corrections, offsetting, refunds
sources.scope: Standard VAT rate charged by VAT-registered persons in KSA.
sources.limitations: Guidance only (Arabic prevails); it explains amendments and does not itself amend the regulation. It contains NO rule specific to construction contracts (progress billing, retention, tax point of works contracts, zero-rating of residential supplies) - those were not found and not assessed. A change after April 2025 is not covered. The 15% appears as the standard rate 'where applicable'.
sources.paraphrase: ZATCA's guideline states VAT-registered persons must charge VAT at a standard rate of 15% where applicable, added to the final sale price. The ZATCA VAT overview page also shows 15% in its rate table.
sources.notes: Evidence file (local, not committed): data/standards/evidence/ZATCA_VAT_Implementing_Regulation_Amendments_Guideline_Issue1_Apr2025.pdf sha256 eeaa3369fd32e0791e51c803776962f7c3f2cda9d26fa82e999f97f74f383757. The rate should still be entered as a governed tax parameter with this source and an effective date, approved by the Commercial Approver. Tax treatment per supply (zero-rated / exempt / reverse charge) needs a tax adviser.

sources.topic: Saudi official public holidays (Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, National Day, Founding Day)
sources.title: HOLIDAYS AND LEAVES (HRSD Knowledge Centre)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (HRSD / MHRSD)
sources.edition_or_publication_date: HRSD Knowledge Centre page authored 15 November 2019 (18 Rabi' Al-Awwal 1441); browser print supplied by the project owner on 2026-10-17 (1 p.)
sources.scope: Private-sector worker entitlement to Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha and National Day holidays and how they interact with weekly rest and leave.
sources.limitations: Labor Law Art. 112 (STD-014) only says paid leave on Eids and occasions 'specified in the Regulations' - the Regulations were not read. Page dates from 2019 and does not mention Founding Day, so Founding Day is NOT verified from a primary document. The user (2026-10-17) stated it is 22 February; this is a user-supplied statement, not a source read - a person should attach the Royal Order or official notice before it is entered as a calendar parameter. Holiday starts depend on the Umm Al-Qura calendar (Eid al-Fitr: the day after 29 Ramadan; Eid al-Adha: from Arafat day; National Day: first day of the month the page calls Libra), so exact dates, any royal-order extensions and annual HRSD / Council of Ministers announcements must be checked each year by a person.
sources.paraphrase: HRSD states workers are entitled to a 4-day Eid al-Fitr holiday starting the day after 29 Ramadan per the Umm Al-Qura calendar, a 4-day Eid al-Adha holiday starting from Arafat day, and the National Day on the first day of Libra, with compensation rules when holidays overlap rest days.
sources.notes: Evidence file (local, not committed): data/standards/evidence/HRSD_Holidays_and_leaves_printed_2026-10-17.pdf sha256 48a687315e1e8fcbcacbfac974c0f194a24c027f240dd5bde4e2a88f6b67cc33. A project calendar MUST be confirmed each year by a human; enter as governed calendar parameters, never as defaults.

sources.topic: Government Tenders and Procurement Law and Implementing Regulations (reference for tender preparation)
sources.title: Government Tenders and Procurement Law (English translation, MoF PDF) - the Law only; the Implementing Regulations were not supplied
sources.edition_or_publication_date: 44-page English text, 99 articles in 7 parts; supersedes the earlier law (Royal Decree M/58 of 4/9/1427H); print stamp '900209 - 22/04/1442'; the Law's own royal-decree number and date are not printed in this PDF. Supplied by the project owner on 2026-10-17.
sources.clause_or_page: Part I General (definitions, principles, scope, advance planning, the Portal, eligibility, tender documents, estimated costs, assessment criteria, divisibility, joint bidding); Part II manner of contracting; Part III proposals and awards (initial guarantee from p.18); Part IV contracts (final guarantee p.27, payments, price adjustment and change orders p.30, subcontracting p.31, fines and extensions, termination, performance assessment); Part V movables; Part VI complaints; Part VII closing; Art. 97 (Regulations), 98 (supersedes M/58), 99 (in force 120 days after publication)
sources.scope: Rules governing government agency tenders, contracting and the Etimad e-portal; context for bid preparation by contractors.
sources.limitations: Only the Law was supplied, not the Implementing Regulations where bid validity, guarantee amounts and deadlines sit. A 05/08/2026 Ministry of Finance news item says Cabinet approved a NEW law, so this text may be superseded; which law and regulations are in force was NOT established. The authority of this English translation was not established. Not used for any cost value; the product must not state procurement-law compliance.
sources.paraphrase: The PDF is the Law's English text: seven parts covering planning and tender documents, ways of contracting (public, limited, two-stage tender, direct purchase, framework agreement, reverse auction), proposals, initial and final guarantees, payments, price adjustment and change orders, subcontracting, fines, termination, and complaints. It leaves the detailed rules (guarantee percentages, deadlines, validity) to Implementing Regulations that are NOT in this file, and Art. 96 refers to local-content regulations.
sources.notes: Evidence file (local, not committed): data/standards/evidence/KSA_Government_Tenders_and_Procurement_Law_EN.pdf sha256 903c14b7a4090f5597f09249d2e377eac74ee98b38bce4177a275b5432d743d1. sources.topic: Saudi Labor Law - hours, rest periods, weekly rest day (Friday), overtime, annual leave (primary text)
sources.title: Labor Law, Royal Decree No. M/51 of 23/8/1426H (27 Sep 2005): English translation by the Bureau of Experts, Council of Ministers; Arabic consolidated text amended through Royal Decree M/44 of 8/2/1446H
sources.publisher: Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers (official translation); Arabic text as supplied
sources.edition_or_publication_date: English: original 2005 text, 'for guidance - the governing text is the Arabic'. Arabic: lists amendments M/24 1434, M/1 1435, M/46 1436, M/14 1440, M/134 1440, M/5 1442, M/44 1446.
sources.clause_or_page: EN Arts. 98-107 (hours, rests, weekly rest, overtime), 109-110 (annual leave), 112-113 (leave); AR Arts. 100, 104-107 cross-checked
sources.scope: Statutory hours, rest, weekly rest day and overtime rules that a project calendar and labour loading must respect.
sources.limitations: Law text only: Executive Regulations, Minister decisions (Art. 99 categories, Art. 106 annual overtime ceiling) and the list of paid Eids/occasions (Art. 112) are separate and were not read. The English file predates later amendments; the Arabic extract was machine-read with garbled spacing, so only Arts. 100, 104, 106, 107 were cross-checked against it. A person must confirm applicability to the project and current amendments. Not a statement of compliance.
sources.paraphrase: Art. 98: max 8 h/day or 48 h/week; Ramadan (Muslims) 6 h/36 h. Art. 99: up to 9 h or down to 7 h by Minister decision. Art. 101: no more than 5 consecutive hours without a 30-min break; max 11 h at workplace. Art. 104: Friday is the weekly rest day for all workers; after notifying the labour office the employer may replace it with another day for some workers; >=24 consecutive hours, full pay, no cash in lieu. Art. 105: remote/continuous work may consolidate rest up to 8 weeks with Ministry approval. Art. 106: exceptions capped at 10 h/day, 60 h/week. Art. 107: overtime = hourly basic wage + 50%; holiday/Eid hours are overtime. Art. 109: annual leave >=21 days.
sources.notes: Evidence files local only (git-ignored); hashes in data/standards/evidence/evidence_manifest.json. The weekly rest day rule was also supplied by the project owner as a secondary-site summary; the primary text above agrees with it.
